conflicts.issue: Aspirational Equity Targets vs. Market Feasibility in the Walltown / Northgate Mall Small Area Plan
conflicts.summary: Committee members differed on whether draft policies calling for 30% affordable housing, affordable retail, and a grocery store risk overpromising to legacy Walltown residents without public subsidy.
conflicts.side_a_position: Keep bold 30% affordability, public open-space, and neighborhood-grid targets in the plan while exploring public tools like TIF or land-value capture to help finance them.
side_a_arguments: Small area plans legitimize years of Walltown organizing and set clear public expectations for phasing and street connectivity.
With public skin in the game—such as state-enabled TIF or LIHTC co-location near an anchored grocery store—the City can help move closer to the 30% goal.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid misleading legacy residents with an aspirational wish list (such as dictating private grocery stores or banning car washes while requiring EV chargers) that government cannot compel under market economics.
side_b_arguments: Durham County's own 500 E Main Street and Shops at Hope Valley experiences show government cannot force private grocers or low-rent retailers to open without 10,000-25,000 monthly foot traffic.
Much of legacy Walltown has already displaced, and putting unfeasible 30% encumbrances on private land risks leaving the mall vacant.
conflicts.resolution: Staff noted they would incorporate phasing and feasibility context while returning revised draft policies in November/December.

conflicts.issue: Pure By-Right Simplicity vs. Opt-In Density Bonuses and Conditional Zoning in the New UDO Draft
conflicts.summary: Members debated whether the new UDO should allow higher missing-middle density unconditionally by right or rely on opt-in bonuses tied to affordability and design safeguards.
conflicts.side_a_position: Minimize extra 'opt-in boxes' and allow the urban density and 15-minute city forms desired by Council cleanly by right.
side_a_arguments: Requiring developers to jump through extra opt-in tiers slows housing supply; as Austin and Minneapolis showed, high supply stabilizes rents.
If Council truly wants walkable density, it should write it straight into base by-right standards.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain opt-in standards, conditional Development Plans, and large-parcel sprawl safeguards so increased density delivers affordability, design quality, and anti-displacement protections.
side_b_arguments: Opt-in options remain by right (skipping 12-18 months of public hearings) while ensuring compact units, active street facades, or affordable percentages are legally secured.
Removing conditional zoning and letting 50-100 acre annexations build purely single-family sprawl undermines complete communities.
conflicts.resolution: Planning Director Sara Young supported keeping opt-in safeguards alongside existing Development Plan/Development Agreement tools and committed to bringing zoning maps and collapsing-district options back to JCCPC.

conflicts.meeting_title: Joint City County Planning Committee September 4, 2024
conflicts.issue: Walltown / Northgate Small Area Plan Advisory Limits and Community Demographic Representation
conflicts.summary: Committee members differed in emphasis regarding how forcefully the Walltown / Northgate Mall Small Area Plan can halt displacement and reflect legacy neighborhood voices versus acknowledging existing gentrification and legal constraints.
conflicts.side_a_position: Leverage City/County zoning, planning, and capital tools collaboratively to realize Walltown coalitions' Northgate Mall vision
side_a_arguments: Walltown Community Association and Northgate Mall Neighborhood Coalition have spent years building an equitable community framework
Collaborative iterative talks with Northwood and experienced mall redevelopers (such as Folger Pratt) can achieve affordable housing and open space
conflicts.side_b_position: Caution residents candidly that a small area plan is non-binding and recognize Walltown's ongoing demographic shift
side_b_arguments: Kickoff survey demographics (56% White vs. 38% Black) show gentrifiers already participate heavily in neighborhood forums
Residents must not be misled into thinking an advisory Small Area Plan provides statutory protection against redevelopment or rising costs
conflicts.resolution: Staff retained both public policy workshops and explicit disclosures regarding advisory legal scope ahead of October and December JCCPC reviews.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee June 6, 2024
conflicts.issue: Public Comment Expectations During Proposed County Commission Reviews of Out-of-UGB Rezonings
conflicts.summary: Committee members agreed to formalize a light-touch County Commission review for rezonings outside the Urban Growth Boundary (UGB) to transmit county service concerns to City Council, but disagreed over whether residents could realistically be prevented from treating the County Commission agenda item as a public hearing.
conflicts.side_a_position: Formalize an informational County Commission review for out-of-UGB rezonings while barring public hearing testimony at the County level and routing resident comments to City Council.
side_a_arguments: Cases outside the UGB affect county services such as EMS, fire stations, and schools and should receive formal County Commission review.
Future Growth Areas inside the UGB are excluded, keeping County Commission reviews rare.
Staff and attorneys can use rules of procedure and clear communication to direct public hearing comments to City Council.
conflicts.side_b_position: Skeptical that placing a rezoning item on a County Commission public agenda without allowing residents to speak is workable in practice.
side_b_arguments: Public pressure from county residents originally prompted the proposal, and residents seeing an item on a public meeting agenda will still expect to speak.
Telling attendees they cannot comment on an agendized development item risks confusion and controversy ('going to be a mess').
conflicts.resolution: Committee gave informal thumbs-up consensus at 01:02:44 to move forward with the out-of-UGB review framework while directing staff and attorneys to clarify public-hearing boundaries.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee - May 1, 2024
conflicts.issue: UDO Public Engagement Survey Representativeness and Direct Affordability Tools
conflicts.summary: Committee members questioned demographic skew in early UDO engagement data and debated how directly the land-use code should tie zoning flexibility to income-restricted affordability and public-land tracking.
conflicts.side_a_position: Broaden outreach beyond high-income/white homeowner survey respondents and embed stronger affordability hooks and public-land strategies in the UDO.
side_a_arguments: Survey demographics heavily skewed toward wealthier homeowners rather than renters and communities of color most affected by displacement.
The UDO rewrite should actively link density bonuses and public-land inventories to tangible income-restricted housing rather than relying solely on market filtering.
conflicts.side_b_position: Use targeted workshops to close outreach gaps while respecting North Carolina statutory limits on mandatory inclusionary zoning.
side_b_arguments: State enabling law prohibits mandatory inclusionary zoning, requiring voluntary incentive-based bonuses and form-based supply expansion.
Simplifying dimensional rules and allowing missing-middle housing types lowers regulatory barriers alongside separate public funding streams.
conflicts.resolution: Staff and Code Studio acknowledged the survey skew and committed to targeted outreach and evaluating voluntary affordability incentives and public-land alignment prior to the 2025 draft UDO.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - December 4, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero convened the December 4, 2024 Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) alongside City Council Members Nate Baker and Mark-Anthony Middleton and County Commissioners, approving the October 2, 2024 minutes unanimously by voice vote. Committee members reviewed the Walltown and Northgate Mall Small Area Plan, emphasizing targets for 20 percent affordable housing (with half serving 30–50% AMI, including a 72-unit senior housing proposal among ~140 total units) and neighborhood park and drainage improvements. Staff also presented proposed Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Use Table restructuring designed to curb quasi-judicial Special Use Permits, simplify zoning districts, and support '15-minute city' neighborhood services, followed by a 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan update from Matt Day projecting 1.5 million additional regional residents and roughly 60,000 needed housing units in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 2, 2024 JCCPC Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero called for approval of the October 2, 2024 JCCPC meeting minutes after confirming City and County committee attendance. Present committee members approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Walltown / Northgate Mall Small Area Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefed JCCPC on community-informed policy drafts for the Walltown and former Northgate Mall site, highlighting targets of 20% affordable housing (half at 30–50% AMI, anchored by a 72-unit senior project toward ~140 affordable units), greenspace, drainage remediation, and transit integration. Members discussed balancing community expectations with redevelopment feasibility and advisory plan limits.

agenda_items.title: UDO Rewrite: Use Table Restructuring and Special Use Permit (SUP) Reform
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined proposed restructuring of the Unified Development Ordinance Use Table to consolidate fragmented use categories, sharply limit quasi-judicial Special Use Permits in favor of clear by-right and design standards, adjust family care home spacing rules, and foster walkable '15-minute city' neighborhood retail.

agenda_items.title: 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) Growth Projections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: MPO Director Matt Day presented long-range 2055 MTP demographic and transportation forecasts showing an additional 1.5 million residents across the Triangle region and roughly 60,000 new housing units needed in Durham, underscoring transit corridor prioritization and multi-modal investment.

votes.notes: Only City Council JCCPC appointees from the seated City roster are listed in ayes; County Commissioners also participated as joint committee members.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved without objection by present JCCPC City Council and County Commissioner members.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee October 2, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Council Member Javiera Caballero, the October 2, 2024 Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) approved June 5 and September 4 minutes and reviewed five major new rezoning cases—highlighting 4802 Cheek Road as the first proposal outside the Urban Growth Boundary. The committee also heard updates on the Heritage Communities Program and engaged in substantive policy debates over market feasibility in the Walltown/Northgate Mall small area plan and whether the new UDO should rely on pure by-right districts or opt-in affordability/design bonuses.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence of Vice Chair Howerton, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero noted Durham County Vice Chair Brenda Howerton's excused absence and led the unanimous approval of minutes from the June 5 and September 4, 2024 JCCPC meetings.

agenda_items.title: New Rezoning Cases Summary (Durham Gateway, Page Corners, Oak Grove, 4802 Cheek Rd, Wake Forest Hwy)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Aaron Cain summarized five new cases plus two non-annexation rezonings, flagging that 4802 Cheek Road (201 units) is the first application submitted outside the Urban Growth Boundary, while Page Corners represents a 100% affordable LIHTC apartment proposal.

agenda_items.title: Walltown Small Area Plan and Former Northgate Mall Site Policies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Carl Plaza presented draft policies for the former Northgate Mall site calling for 20-30% affordable housing, affordable grocery/retail, public spaces, and tree canopy to cool an urban heat island. Northwood owner Sandy Spurgeon and attorney Nil Ghosh asked for phased feasibility flexibility, while Middleton and Commissioner Jacobs cautioned against misleading residents with unrealistic market promises vs. Baker urging public TIF/land-value capture.

agenda_items.title: Heritage Communities Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planners Carla Rosenberg and Anna-Christina Hoffman outlined non-regulatory recognition for 50+-year historic communities featuring council resolutions, $2,500 interpretive signs funded by the department, GIS story maps, and County Library archives.

agenda_items.title: New Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Draft Zoning Districts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Bo Dobrzenski presented Code Studio's consolidated draft districts—including Residential Preserve (3-acre outside UGB), Residential Diverse (5,000 sq ft minimum with compact and affordable opt-ins), RX3/RX5/RX8, CX3/CX5/CX8/CX20, Industrial Mixed Use, and Conservation—sparking debate on pure by-right density versus opt-in bonuses and greenfield conditional zoning.

agenda_items.title: 2025 Monthly JCCPC Schedule and Chair/Vice Chair Rotation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Sara Young recommended returning to monthly meetings starting January 8, 2025 (skipping July 2025) for UDO workload, and Chair Caballero noted the January rotation naming Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as Chair and Council Member Nate Baker as Vice Chair.

votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee meeting chaired by Javiera Caballero; County Commissioner Vice Chair Brenda Howerton had an excused absence; observed participants included Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Nate Baker, County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, and County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns.

meetings.title: Joint City County Planning Committee September 4, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Council Member Javiera Caballero alongside City Council Members Nate Baker and Mark-Anthony Middleton plus Durham County Commissioners, the September 4, 2024 JCCPC session held three major planning policy briefings with no formal committee votes. Senior Planner Carl Kolosna updated the committee on the Walltown / Northgate Mall Small Area Plan (59 June kickoff attendees, 201 comments, draft 19 policies, 68 acres), sparking a substantive exchange between Baker—who urged public-private support for community-led redevelopment—and Middleton, who cautioned that Walltown demographics have already gentrified (56% White / 38% Black kickoff survey split) and stressed honesty that small-area plans are non-binding. Senior Planner Kayla Seibel presented a revised Page-Miami Design District (formerly RTP South) transit-oriented rezoning proposal keeping Davis Park residential/mixed-use development plans intact while applying Compact Suburban Design districts on the east side and flagging a Family Fare gas station exclusion request for Planning Commission review. Planning staff Lisa Miller and Bo also outlined four engagement phases and Dr. Tawana Allen's Engagement Ambassadors program for the new UDO.

agenda_items.title: Walltown and Former Northgate Mall Small Area Plan Draft Policy Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Carl Kolosna reported on the June 29 Walltown kickoff (59 attendees, 201 comments, 68-acre Northgate site, 9 city-owned vacant lots, paper alleys, and flooding concerns) and release of 19 draft policies following Northwood's submitted-and-withdrawn rezoning application. Council Member Baker advocated aligning City/County tools behind the community vision, while Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton cautioned on gentrified participation demographics and clarified the advisory legal limits of a small area plan.

agenda_items.title: Page-Miami Design District (Formerly RTP South) Transit-Oriented Rezoning Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Kayla Seibel presented a revised rezoning map for the Page-Miami corridor after resident outreach, shifting from blanket Compact Suburban Design (CSD) to CSD Core and Support-1 east of the rail line near the relocated GoTriangle regional transit hub while retaining Davis Park's RC/RUM/mixed-use zoning and proposing Commercial Neighborhood (CN) for a vacant retail parcel. Committee members advised against carving out a Family Fare gas station from CSD Core to preserve long-term transit-oriented redevelopment.

agenda_items.title: New Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Phased Community Engagement & Engagement Ambassadors
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefed JCCPC on Code Studio's technical modules and four phased engagement waves starting Fall 2024 across county libraries, office hours, and Dr. Tawana Allen's (TG Allen & Associates) Engagement Ambassadors program targeting 30+ focus groups. Council Member Baker asked about tying cross-street cross-sections from Public Works into Module 3, and Chair Caballero emphasized stronger outreach to refugee and non-English-speaking residents.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - August 7, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The August 7, 2024 Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) meeting failed to convene due to a lack of quorum. After waiting on additional members at 00:01:11, 00:06:23, and 00:08:44 while attempting to reach absent committee members, the speaker announced at 00:28:26 that quorum had still not been achieved. To prevent delaying the committee's work until its next scheduled October meeting, the official stated that members would receive follow-up communication from the chair or Planning Director Sara Young to tentatively reschedule the meeting for Wednesday, September 4, 2024 at 9:30 a.m.

agenda_items.title: Quorum Check, Cancellation Due to Lack of Quorum, and Tentative Rescheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and the presiding member waited from 00:01:11 through 00:28:26 for enough JCCPC members to arrive and contacted absent members to establish a quorum. At 00:28:26, the speaker announced that quorum could not be reached, noted the meeting could not formally adjourn because it never convened, and indicated that Director Sara Young or the chair would follow up to schedule a September make-up meeting—tentatively Wednesday, September 4 at 9:30 a.m.—rather than waiting until October.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee June 6, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The June 6, 2024 Joint City-County Planning Committee meeting approved its minutes by voice vote and received two staff presentations from the City-County Planning Department: updated neighborhood meeting guidelines shaped by 282 community comments and a demonstration of the new GIS-based Durham Rezoning Explorer replacing Social Pinpoint. Members then debated a proposal to formalize County Commission work-session reviews for rare rezoning applications located outside the Urban Growth Boundary. While committee members informally agreed to advance the light-touch review process without triggering public hearings at the County Commission, Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton warned that barring public comment on an agendized item would prove difficult in practice.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero called the meeting to order and conducted roll call with Vice Chair Hamilton, Commissioners Cameron, Burns, and Jacobs, Council Member Nate Baker, and Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton present. No agenda adjustments or manager priority items were raised, and the committee approved its prior minutes by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Meeting Guidelines Update and Active Cases Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Business Services Analyst Justin Henderson presented four revisions to neighborhood meeting guidelines based on 282 community comments and benchmarking against Raleigh and Cary: shifting initial legislative neighborhood meetings to within 30 days after application submittal, requiring a second meeting after staff review and before Planning Commission, mandating posted site signage, and barring scheduling conflicts with governing body or Planning Commission meetings. Committee members discussed future neutral facilitation, tailored outreach such as Spanish-language materials, and small-project waivers (such as single-family homes and duplexes), and staff briefly updated members on two active cases (Dr. Nichols Town's 25 townhouses and 5052 Wake Forest Highway).

agenda_items.title: Durham Rezoning Explorer Demonstration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Business System Analyst Chris Peterson demonstrated the Durham Rezoning Explorer, a new City-County GIS application built to replace the deactivated Social Pinpoint platform. The tool displays rezoning and annexation details, current and proposed zoning, review milestones, and enables residents to submit public comments with overnight database updates.

agenda_items.title: County Commission Review Process for Rezonings Outside the Urban Growth Boundary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members and Planning Director Sara Young discussed creating a formal, non-binding County Commission work-session review for rare rezoning cases outside the Urban Growth Boundary (excluding Future Growth Areas inside the boundary) to flag county service impacts such as EMS, fire, and schools before City Council's public hearing. Members gave informal thumbs-up consensus to proceed while emphasizing that County Commission review must be communicated as informational rather than a public hearing.

votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee vote; listed ayes reflect the seated City Council members on the committee who participated alongside Durham County Commissioners.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Javiera Caballero called for a motion and second to approve the minutes; members responded aye with none opposed.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee - May 1, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) met on May 1, 2024 to excuse Nate Baker's absence and review a comprehensive update and Code Audit for the New Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) rewrite led by Code Studio. Consultant Bo Dobrzynski outlined structural simplifications including consolidating 15+ articles into 10, merging overlapping single-family districts, adopting form- and height-based zoning nomenclature (e.g., CX-3/5/8), and running economic feasibility pro-formas for Expanded Housing Choices ahead of public drafts in early 2025. Committee members debated demographic skew in the public engagement survey and how directly the UDO can integrate inclusionary affordability and publicly controlled land.

agenda_items.title: Attendance and Motion to Excuse Nate Baker
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero convened the Joint City County Planning Committee with City Council members Mark-Anthony Middleton and Leonardo Williams alongside County Commissioners Howerton and Jacobs and Planning Commission Chair Cameron. The committee voted unanimously to excuse the absence of Council Member Nate Baker.

agenda_items.title: New UDO Rewrite Update and Code Audit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Code Studio consultant Bo Dobrzynski and Planning staff presented the New UDO Code Audit, proposing to streamline over 15 articles into 10, consolidate legacy residential districts (RU-5, RU-5(2), RS-8, RS-10), replace density caps with height- and form-based district labels (such as CX-3, CX-5, and CX-8), and model financial feasibility for Expanded Housing Choices ahead of February-March 2025 public drafts. Mayor Williams and County Commissioner Howerton challenged demographic overrepresentation in engagement survey responses and pressed for tracking publicly owned land and affordable housing outcomes inside the code.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee - May 1, 2024
disagreements.issue: UDO Public Engagement Survey Representativeness and Direct Affordability Tools
disagreements.summary: Committee members questioned demographic skew in early UDO engagement data and debated how directly the land-use code should tie zoning flexibility to income-restricted affordability and public-land tracking.
disagreements.side_a_position: Broaden outreach beyond high-income/white homeowner survey respondents and embed stronger affordability hooks and public-land strategies in the UDO.
side_a_arguments: Survey demographics heavily skewed toward wealthier homeowners rather than renters and communities of color most affected by displacement.
The UDO rewrite should actively link density bonuses and public-land inventories to tangible income-restricted housing rather than relying solely on market filtering.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use targeted workshops to close outreach gaps while respecting North Carolina statutory limits on mandatory inclusionary zoning.
side_b_arguments: State enabling law prohibits mandatory inclusionary zoning, requiring voluntary incentive-based bonuses and form-based supply expansion.
Simplifying dimensional rules and allowing missing-middle housing types lowers regulatory barriers alongside separate public funding streams.
disagreements.resolution: Staff and Code Studio acknowledged the survey skew and committed to targeted outreach and evaluating voluntary affordability incentives and public-land alignment prior to the 2025 draft UDO.
